provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Movement skills
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate running, jumping, hopping and skipping movements.
The pupils should be able to participate in a relay race.
Introduction:
Today we will learn different ways to move our bodies like when we play in the compound or during break time.
These movements help us stay strong and healthy.
Content:
Running is moving fast on your feet like when you are late for school.
Jumping is pushing off the ground with both feet at the same time.
Hopping is jumping on one foot like when we cross a small puddle.
Skipping is hopping on one foot while swinging the other leg forward.
In relay practice, we pass a baton to our friends while running in a team.
Class activity:
The teacher will divide the class into four teams for a relay race using a stick as the baton.
Evaluation questions:
What do we use to pass in a relay race?
Show me how to hop on one foot.
Name two ways we can move our bodies.
Summary:
Today we learned different movement skills that help us stay active and work together in teams.

topics.title: Ball skills
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to throw and catch a ball properly.
The pupils should be able to bounce a ball.
Introduction:
We use balls when we play in the school field or during our games period.
Today we will learn how to handle balls correctly.
Content:
Throwing is sending the ball through the air to someone else.
Catching is receiving the ball with your hands when it comes to you.
Bouncing is hitting the ball on the ground so it goes up and down.
In circle games, we stand in a circle and pass the ball around.
We can play games like "who is my neighbor" with a ball.
Class activity:
The pupils will form a circle and practice passing a ball around while singing a song.
Evaluation questions:
What do we do to receive a ball?
Show me how to bounce a ball.
Name one game we can play with a ball in a circle.
Summary:
Today we learned important ball skills that help us play games safely and have fun with friends.

topics.title: Fitness basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to perform basic warm-up exercises.
The pupils should be able to explain why exercise safety is important.
Introduction:
Before we play any sport or run around, we need to prepare our bodies.
Today we will learn how to stay safe while exercising.
Content:
Warm up is preparing our bodies for exercise by moving slowly.
Stretching is making our muscles longer to prevent injury.
Exercise safety means not pushing our bodies too hard too quickly.
We should always wear proper shoes when exercising.
We should drink water after exercise to stay hydrated.
Class activity:
The teacher will lead the class in a simple warm-up routine including stretches and light jogging.
Evaluation questions:
Why do we warm up before exercise?
Show me how to stretch your arms.
What should we do after exercising?
Summary:
Today we learned how to prepare our bodies for exercise and stay safe while being active.

topics.title: Personal health
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list proper bathing and brushing techniques.
The pupils should be able to identify clean clothes.
Introduction:
Keeping ourselves clean helps us stay healthy and avoid getting sick.
Today we will learn about good personal hygiene habits.
Content:
Bathing means washing our bodies with soap and water every day.
Brushing our teeth means cleaning them with a toothbrush and toothpaste.
Clean clothes are fresh clothes that we wear after washing them.
Health habits chart helps us remember to do these things every day.
We should wash our hands before eating food after playing outside.
Class activity:
The pupils will draw a health habits chart showing when to bathe, brush teeth and change clothes.
Evaluation questions:
How often should we bathe?
What do we use to clean our teeth?
Why is it important to wear clean clothes?
Summary:
Today we learned about personal hygiene habits that help us stay healthy and clean.

topics.title: Food and health
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify healthy foods.
The pupils should be able to name examples of junk food.
Introduction:
The food we eat affects how we feel and how our bodies work.
Today we will learn about healthy foods and those we should eat less of.
Content:
Healthy foods give us energy and help us grow strong.
Examples include rice, beans, vegetables, fruits and fish.
Junk foods are high in sugar and fat but not very healthy.
Examples include ice cream, sugary drinks, biscuits and sweet snacks.
We should eat more healthy foods and less junk food.
Class activity:
The pupils will sort pictures of different foods into healthy and junk food categories.
Evaluation questions:
Name one healthy food you eat at home.
What is junk food?
Why should we eat more healthy foods?
Summary:
Today we learned that eating healthy foods helps us grow strong and stay healthy.

topics.title: Safety at home
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify dangers of sharp objects and fire.
The pupils should be able to list home safety rules.
Introduction:
Our homes should be safe places where we feel protected.
Today we will learn about staying safe from dangers at home.
Content:
Sharp objects like knives and scissors can cut us if we are not careful.
Fire can burn us and destroy our things if we get too close.
Home safety rules include not playing with matches or lighters.
We should tell an adult if we find something dangerous at home.
We should keep away from the kitchen when cooking is happening.
Class activity:
The pupils will role-play different scenarios showing how to respond to dangers at home.
Evaluation questions:
What can happen if we play with fire?
Name one sharp object we should be careful with.
What should you do if you find something dangerous?
Summary:
Today we learned important safety rules to keep us safe from dangers at home.

topics.title: Games: tag and dodge
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to play tag and dodge games fairly.
The pupils should be able to follow game rules.
Introduction:
Games are fun ways to stay active and make friends.
Today we will learn how to play tag and dodge games properly.
Content:
In tag games, one person is "it" and tries to touch others.
When you are tagged, you become "it" and continue the game.
In dodge games, we try to avoid being hit by a ball or object.
Playing fair means following the rules and not cheating.
Following rules makes the game fun for everyone.
Class activity:
The teacher will organize a game of "freeze tag" where tagged players must stand still until freed.
Evaluation questions:
What happens when you are tagged in tag games?
Why is it important to play fair?
Name one rule in dodge games.
Summary:
Today we learned how to play tag and dodge games fairly while following the rules.

topics.title: Athletics: short races
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate proper starting and finishing techniques.
The pupils should be able to participate in a 50 metre dash.
Introduction:
Running races is a fun way to test our speed and strength.
Today we will learn how to run short races properly.
Content:
The 50 metre dash is a short race where we run as fast as we can.
Starting means getting ready to run when the teacher blows the whistle.
Finishing means crossing the line with your chest first.
We should run on the balls of our feet for better speed.
We should practice running straight without zigzagging.
Class activity:
The pupils will practice starting positions and then run a 50 metre dash on the school field.
Evaluation questions:
What signal tells us to start running?
Show me how to finish a race properly.
Why should we run on the balls of our feet?
Summary:
Today we learned how to run short races with good starting and finishing techniques.

topics.title: First aid basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to treat small cuts and bruises.
The pupils should be able to know when to tell an adult.
Introduction:
Sometimes we get small injuries while playing or at home.
Today we will learn basic first aid for minor injuries.
Content:
Small cuts are small breaks in our skin that may bleed a little.
Bruises are marks on our skin that turn purple or blue when bumped.
For small cuts, we should wash with clean water and cover with a plaster.
For bruises, we should apply a cold cloth to reduce swelling.
We should always tell an adult about any injury we get.
Class activity:
The pupils will practice treating a small cut on a doll using clean water and a bandage.
Evaluation questions:
What should we do for a small cut?
How do we treat a bruise?
When should we tell an adult about an injury?
Summary:
Today we learned basic first aid for small injuries and when to seek help from adults.

topics.title: Revision and sports day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to participate in class mini sports.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate skills learned during the term.
Introduction:
Today we will remember all the things we learned this term and have fun.
We will show our skills in different activities.
Content:
Class mini sports include running races, ball games and relay races.
We will show how to run, jump, throw and catch properly.\Certificates will be given to pupils who try their best.
Sports day is a time to celebrate our physical abilities.
We should cheer for our friends and play fairly.
Class activity:
The class will be divided into teams for mini sports competitions including sack race and egg and spoon race.
Evaluation questions:
Name one skill we learned this term.
What should we do during sports day?
Why is it important to play fairly?
Summary:
Today we practiced our skills and had fun during mini sports while remembering to play fairly.
